sentenceSets.sentence: His animus toward the opposing party was personal as well as political, rooted in decades of rivalry.

answerChoices.reasoning: Indifference means lack of feeling; the animus rooted in decades of rivalry shows deep negative feeling, not indifference.
Respect means regard or esteem; animus is spiteful and malevolent ill will, the opposite of respect.
Camaraderie means friendly fellowship; animus rooted in personal and political rivalry contradicts camaraderie.
Uncertainty means doubt; the animus is deep-rooted prejudiced ill will, not doubt or uncertainty of feeling.
Concern means worry or care; while the person cares about opposition, animus specifies prejudiced spiteful ill will.
Skepticism means doubt; the animus is malevolent prejudiced hostility, not mere doubt.
Disagreement means differing views; rooted in decades of rivalry, animus involves spiteful ill will beyond disagreement.
Enmity means hostility between rivals, which fits the decades of rivalry context, but lacks the specific prejudicial malevolence that animus implies.
Admiration means regard and approval; animus is malevolent ill will rooted in rivalry, the opposite.
Affection means fondness; animus toward an opposing party based on decades of rivalry indicates hatred.
Loyalty means faithful allegiance; while political stance might involve loyalty, animus specifies personal prejudiced ill will.

sentenceSets.sentence: The reviewer's animus against experimental literature was evident in the harshly dismissive tone of every critique, regardless of individual merit.

answerChoices.reasoning: Expertise means skill or knowledge; the animus against a literary form indicates prejudice, not expert judgment.
Objectivity means impartiality; the animus evident in every critique regardless of merit shows prejudice, not objectivity.
Curiosity means interest in learning; animus against experimental literature indicates closed-mindedness, not curiosity.
Appreciation means recognition of value; animus that dismisses every experimental work shows lack of appreciation.
Skepticism means doubt; while the reviewer doubts experimental literature, animus specifies spiteful prejudiced ill will.
Caution means careful wariness; the animus involves prejudiced hostility, not cautious restraint.
Discernment means ability to judge wisely; animus that dismisses regardless of merit indicates prejudice, not wise judgment.
Bias means unfair prejudice toward or against something; while bias captures the prejudicial nature, animus adds the specific element of malevolent ill will.
Enthusiasm means eager interest; animus against experimental literature is hostile, the opposite of enthusiastic engagement.
Admiration means regarding with approval; the harshly dismissive animus indicates contempt, not admiration.
Fairness means treating impartially; animus evident regardless of individual merit shows prejudice, not fairness.

sentenceSets.sentence: The employee's animus toward her supervisor was so pronounced that she challenged every decision, even sensible ones, out of pure spite.

answerChoices.reasoning: Loyalty means allegiance and support; challenging decisions out of pure spite indicates hostility, not loyalty.
Respect means holding in esteem; animus causing her to challenge even sensible decisions shows disrespect and ill will.
Deference means polite respect; animus causing her to challenge decisions demonstrates the opposite of respectful deference.
Cooperation means working together; animus causing her to oppose decisions shows inability or unwillingness to cooperate.
Concern means worry about quality; the animus involves spiteful opposition regardless of decision quality.
Caution means careful wariness; the animus involves prejudiced hostility, not cautious evaluation.
Doubt means uncertainty; challenging sensible decisions indicates animus or spite, not reasonable doubt.
Tension describes strained relations; while present between supervisor and employee, tension is a condition, not the malevolent ill will that animus represents.
Admiration means approval and respect; challenging every decision due to animus shows contempt, not admiration.
Affection means fondness or liking; animus toward the supervisor is hostile ill will, the opposite.
Trust means confidence and faith; animus causing opposition to even sensible decisions shows lack of trust.
